utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Gotovina et al. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning to you as well, Mr. Cvrk. I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony yesterday. Are you ready to proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, may have I document P610, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvrk, good morning.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, yesterday at the point of adjournment we were discussing the disciplinary authority of the chief of police administration, and you rejected the statement made by Mr. Cetina that I put to you last evening. Now, if you look at this document, this actually I called up yesterday but we didn't deal with it. This is an order issued by General Mladen Markac to the commander of the special police unit attached to the Dubrovnik-Neretva Police Administration, and he is ordered to investigate into the conduct of a member of his unit and to initiate disciplinary proceedings. And you -- do you note that this order is sent to the chief of the police administration asking him to hand it over to the commander of the special police unit. The chief of police is not asked to order the special police unit commander, but he is asked to hand this order which is a direct order from General Markac to the commander of the special police unit. And if you would see in the last paragraph, the commander of the special police unit is asked to report back to the police -- special police sector on the disciplinary measures taken. So do you agree with me that the contents of this document, in fact, reflects that -- what Mr. Cetina said about his disciplinary authority over the special police unit attached to his police administration is correct? This is consistent with what he said?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to object to the question because there's been no foundation that the Dubrovnik police administration is under Mr. Cetina's authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that is not the issue. The issue is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please rephrase your question so that the issue remains what you think the issue is and that ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Does this reflect -- isn't it correct that General Markac, in fact, had the ability to order the special police unit commanders attached to police administration directly to initiate disciplinary authority and that that did not fall within the competence of the chief of the police administration?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with your assertion, Mrs. Prosecutor, for several reasons. The document that you have shown here is, beyond any doubt, an authentic document, which was signed by the assistant minister, Mr. Mladen Markac. The gist of it is this: This is a member of the Dubrovnik-Neretva Police Administration who was engaged in a mission which was at the state level, I believe, because he was dispatched to the Neum state border. I'm not sure whether it falls within the Neretva-Dubrovnik area or not. But I know that members of my unit were also tasked with the same mission that these members of the Neretva-Dubrovnik Police Administration were. It is stated here that an Official Note was made of an incident which happened on the 15th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there. What apparently Ms. Mahindaratne wants to know is whether the authority which is expressed here in this order, whether that's more consistent with what another witness said than what you say. You're now explaining all the specific circumstances. Would circumstances just disturb the authority or would it not? The authorities who can order disciplinary measures or disciplinary investigations to take place, would that be different, any way different in Dubrovnik-Neretva Police Administration compared to any other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I merely wanted to explain the circumstances under which the disciplinary measure was imposed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm taking you back to what -- what the question was about. Was the authority, in view of ordering that disciplinary investigations should take place, any different in Dubrovnik-Neretva Police Administration compared to the others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The procedure involved is one where assistant minister of the interior, based on information received, may ask that disciplinary proceedings be initiated. In the case where a member of the Dubrovnik-Neretva Police Administration is concerned, the disciplinary proceedings can only be initiated before a disciplinary court of the Dubrovnik-Neretva Police Administration. The same would apply to any other member of any other police administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Carefully listen to the next question Ms. Mahindaratne will put to you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, isn't it correct, Mr. Cvrk, that you came within the command structure of your chief of police administration only when you assisted him in police operations that were conducted within the -- the regular police operations conducted within the police administration area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the priority method of proceeding on the part of any police force of any police administration, and it was the basic way in which the Ministry of Interior worked.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: My question was very clear. Isn't it correct that you came within the command structure of your chief of police administration only when you assisted him in regular police work which was carried out within his area of police administration? That is the only circumstances. That is my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: He answered the question. And a repeating of the question is not appropriate. He has answered the question. That was the priority method of proceeding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, whether that is -- Ms. Mahindaratne is entitled to further explore whether command structures are expressed by way of preference or -- which is highly uncommon, I would say. That was a -- preferably my command would be this one or that one. Therefore, Ms. Mahindaratne is entitled to further explore the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I do understand that, Your Honour. But to ask the exact same question again is really inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's why I said that she can further explore the matter, Mr. Kuzmanovic. And Ms. Mahindaratne will certainly have understood that putting exactly the same question is not a way of exploring a matter any further. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, may I also point out that I think there is a practice in this Court that generally when a counsel cross-examines or examines a witness it is that counsel who rises to their feet to object. This is -- perhaps this has happened before, and I think the Trial Chamber has pointed out that this is not appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Some self-restraint is, to use the word, is preferred. Mr. Kuzmanovic, and in view of the number of objections and in view of the effect which has been shown, I think that you should not forget about self-restraint.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have absolutely no problem with that. I guess I need to do whatever I think is appropriate to defend the interests of our client, and I will do that with the Court's guidance, of course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you answer my question, Mr. Cvrk. My question is that the only circumstances under which you would come within the command -- subordination of the police -- chief of police administration is when you assist him in regular police work which are carried out within the area of the police administration. Is that a yes or a no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is yes. I was a member of the Zagreb Police Administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, isn't it correct that in the case of a crime committed by a member of your unit, General Markac had the capacity to order you directly to investigate the crime without seeking the assistance of the MUP crime police to investigate the matter, since the special police itself was a police force?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not the case. General Markac would have had to insist on the imposition of disciplinary measures, in case they had not been imposed before, because he was the one who was the number one in the chain of command and he received information to that effect. Since he was at the top of the chain of command, he could have asked from each and every one of the police structures to initiate disciplinary proceedings. Disciplinary proceedings were carried out before disciplinary courts in each and every police administration and, in the second instance, before the disciplinary court in the Ministry of Interior. I said that there was also a higher instances where the complaint or the appellant could have addressed the administrative court of the Republic of Croatia, and if the person was still dissatisfied with the judgement handed down, he could have addressed the Supreme Court of the Republic of Croatia, and that was the extent of the legal remedies in relation to breaches of discipline.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvrk, I think you understood my question. My question was: In the case of a crime committed by a member of your unit, General Markac had the capacity to order you to investigate the crime, as in carry out the tasks that the crime police would do, without really seeking the assistance of the crime police, because the special police had the capacity to investigate the crime. I'm talking about crime investigations.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam Prosecutor, my unit which provided the most assistance in all sort of policing work did not have or keep the so-called K register which would stand for the crime register. We could have assisted the work of the crime police, but we did not engage in criminal investigation. If a member of the special police of the Ministry of the Interior committed a crime, just as any other citizen of the Republic of Croatia, he would have be the subject of the criminal investigation on the part of the crime police force of the Ministry of Interior. We were not engaged in criminal inquiries, regardless of the fact that we were authorised personnel. Why? Well, because there was the criminal investigation police to do that job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvrk, there is malcommunication at this moment. You are explaining what usually was done. Ms. Mahindaratne asks you whether Mr. Markac had the authority, whether he used that authority is a different matter for the time being, but whether he had the authority to order you to investigate a crime committed by a member of your unit. That's the question, not what happened, but whether he had the authority. Could you answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, General Markac did have the authority to ask that disciplinary proceedings be initiated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- why do you give an answer different? We are talking about crimes and about investigation of crimes. If you would say that's covered by what I said, fine. Then that's on the record. But that was the question. I didn't ask you whether he had the authority to -- to initiate disciplinary proceedings. My question was whether he had the authority to order you to investigate when a crime was committed by a member of your unit. Would you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Generally speaking, if he had notice of it, he had the authority to initiate proceedings of any form. That's the extent of it. Going back to the question put by the Prosecution, relating to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- criminal investigation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say he had the authority to initiate. That means also to order an investigation when a crime was committed. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, it is very difficult to answer the question with a yes or a no, because there was a direct responsibility to be borne under General Markac on the shoulders of the specialist branches. However, from this particular example, it is quite visible that if he had notice of anything going on at the level of the ministry, he did have the authority to ask for the proceedings to be initiated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, including a crime to be investigated. And he could order you to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the sense of proceedings, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would investigation of a crime, would that be included in what you call "proceedings"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please carefully listen to the next question Ms. Mahindaratne will put to you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvrk, moving on to another area. I just wanted to, before that, just seek a clarification. Yesterday when Mr. Mikulicic showed you a document and asked you if you had seen it before, you said you had seen it during preparation for testimony. Now, how many times did you meet with the Defence team in preparation for testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I was first contacted roughly two years ago. We had slightly more contacts around the time I was giving my statement. And since I already been here before but there was some rescheduling, so I was here on two occasions and I had, each time, one day of proofing.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And during those times, were you shown documents, apart from the one you said you had already seen yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at any rate, some of the documents which had to do with the preparation and execution of Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Were you shown orders of Mr. Markac?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the orders, yes. But I was aware of these documents back at the time when I was commander of the special police unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Were you shown photographs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you have in mind specifically. There were several photographs.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking. You were shown certain photographs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Were you told that those photographs were already in evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: If I recollect correctly, I believe they did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Were you shown photographs of special police taken in Gracac at some stage, just after the operation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely those photographs.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Were you -- did the Defence team discuss any evidence led in these proceedings with you? Any other -- for any other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in that sense, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And when you were here, you said you had been to The Hague before. Were you listening to or following the proceedings that were going on at the time in court?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Periodically, yes, whenever I was able to, over the Internet. As for the testimonies, the last testimony I followed was the one by Mr. Davorin Pavlovic, upon my returned to Zagreb, the little that I could glean.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that. Now, going to Operation Storm, just one question before that. Before the war - and when I say that, I'm talking about the period before the -- the Krajina came under the control of the RSK authorities - did you live in any part of the territory through which you and your unit conducted operations, in the course of Operation Storm or in the course of the mop-up operations afterwards?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was born in Osijek, and most of my family are there. My parents are in Slavonia, and that means that I'm not really connected to the area where Operation Storm was conducted in any significant way.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Were there any other members in your unit who were from the area, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, the unit was multi-ethnic from its very set-up, so that there were both Croats and Serbs within the unit who were from this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, at the pre-operation briefings, either prior to the commencement of Operation Storm itself or the mop-up operations, were you given any information as to which of the villages, through which your unit moved, advanced, as to which of those villages were Croat villages or which were Serb villages? Were you given that information?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Similarly to the attitude to the members of my unit, which came from several ethnicities, in terms of their origin, my attitude to them was like to any citizens of the Republic of Croatia; my attitude to the area that we were liberating was an attitude to the territory of the Republic of Croatia. The villages which mostly were populated by one or the other ethnicity -- this was not very important when we carried out our tasks. Only when considering the size of the places, it could be expected that considerable military forces were there or that straggling enemy soldiers might be in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvrk, you didn't quite answer my question. My question was not about your attitude. Whether any information was given to you as to what villages on the -- on the route, you know, through your axis, were Croat villages or what were Serbs, whether that information was provided to you by any -- either the special police sector command or the inner control branch, any intelligence information. That was my question. Is that a yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: In that sense, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Going to mop-up operations, Mr. Cvrk, I'd like to take you to your statement given to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And this is at D1833, paragraph 21. This is in the English document at paragraph 21, starts at page 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: But I'm going to read to you part of that paragraph. You say: "As far as I know, there were several occasions when combat contact occurred with members of the remaining terrorist groups during ground search operations. Several enemy soldiers were taken prisoner, and significant amounts of MES, minefields, weapons, and equipment were discovered." Now, yesterday, also you testified about such fire contact.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And, for the record, this is at t -- transcript reference number T5384 and -- sorry, 25384 and 25388, where you discuss combat activity with the enemy in the course of mop-up operations. Now, these mop-up -- combat activity that you referred to, did those occur in the course of the series of mop-up operations carried out by the special police during the period 21st and 3rd September? I'm referring to the operations which were known as Action Oluja-Obruc.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to my knowledge, there were such contacts.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now did your unit, the Zagreb Unit, meet with fire contact with the enemy during the operations carried out between 21st August and 3rd September?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no. But this is in the reports that we had to submit. We submitted daily reports. And as far as I remember, I think we mostly found mines and explosives as well as civilians and persons who were supposed to be possibly members of the military and who were then delivered to the regular police for further procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, when say to your knowledge -- your previous answer was to your knowledge there was such contacts. So obviously you are referring to, then, other units. What other units met with fire contact, to your knowledge? Are you able to tell the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: It is difficult to me to assert that with any certainty what was the number of such contacts that occurred, but according to knowledge I had at the time, as we communicated among ourselves, I know that such contacts did occur, and that there was a number of units who reported that kind of contacts to the special police sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, apart from the Lucko Unit, are you aware of any other units that met with fire contact? You said there were several other units.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: If I tried to answer exactly about any of these, I couldn't say that precisely. I know that there were such contacts, but what other units except the one from Lucko had such contacts, I'm not really sure, because a long time has passed since.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you said, you know, prisoners were taken during these operations. Did your unit take any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that one of the attached documents talks about that, about one person who was found where my unit was engaged. And it was supposed that he was a JNA officer, and then he was delivered for further procedure. The unit frequently entered settlements where there were some civilians, fewer or more numerous in number, and then, depending on whether they were registered or not, we decided what needed to be done so that they would be registered. We also reported about their needs, especially if they were elderly and weak, so that they could be helped through the UNHCR and the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, could, we try to find out what the witness remembers and what he says -- what documents are talking about. What you just told us, is that your recollection, or is it just that you read those documents and that you find it in those documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's partly my recollection, and partly it comes from the original documents which were submitted to the special police sector on behalf of my unit and personally on my own behalf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you tell what you say is your own recollection and what is taken from the documents?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the statement, I gave my statement mostly from my recollection. But during the proofing, the Defence reminded me of the original documents which were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... needs to be restarted, so we should have patience for a second. We have restarted the system. We were exploring what was your own recollection and what was -- in your answer, referring to the documents, you're talking about one person who was supposed to be a JNA officer. Were you present when this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that they reported to me about that person, because it was in the general area of Knin. And then, later on, the members of the unit sent this person for further processing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Further processing meaning exactly what in this context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Establishing his personal data, personal identity, confirmation of his identity; and I believe that then the procedure would be divided, whether it was a civilian, in which case civilian police would continue that; or if it could be established that that was military personnel, then he would be handed over for further procedure to the military police. So this was the general procedure applied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This one supposed JNA officer, was he found to be a civilian or a military man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That happened during the later procedure, and then we did not have much connection with that. We just found this person, and we sent him for further proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you were asked whether any prisoners were taken. From your answer now, I take it that one person was processed, because he supposedly was a JNA officer, although you do not know what the results were of further verification of this idea, and that this is the kind of thing that happened with others which were found in settlements that it was verified whether they were registered or not, and that you would decide what to do. That's not really what I understand to be prisoners taken. But it sounds to me as if you were verifying the status - civilian or military - of persons you found and that you give one example where there was a suspicion that someone was a JNA officer and that was processed but you do not know what the outcome was. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time, during the Oluja-Obruc, in case of this particular person, he was taken into custody, and then he was handed over to others for further procedure in order to establish his personal data. There were other persons for whom it was quite simple to determine what their personal data were. There were persons whose personal data needed to be further established. If further establishment was necessary, then our duty was just to take these persons into custody. And that was the procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Even if the result could be that they finally were found to be civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, eventually it was so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what apparently Ms. Mahindaratne wanted to know is - at least that's how I understood your question - whether any persons were taken prisoner, who then finally were found to be non-civilians or non-combatants. Is that what you were ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, could you give us any example of someone taken into custody who turned out to be a -- not a civilian, a combatant, or whatever you found. Tell us what you know about it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apart from the -- my general recollection of the events from 15 years ago, during the proofing, there were several reports relating to the activities of the unit that I commanded, and from these reports, which are enclosed, together with my statement, enclosed by the Defence, it is visible from them that they were person who were established on the spot to be such persons. It is obvious from my reports that they were persons taken into custody and persons who's personal identity was established immediately. I do not know if there were any persons whom we had taken into custody and for whom it was found out later that they were military personnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I asked you these questions because I want to find out exactly what your personal recollection of matters is and what is to be deduced from documentary evidence. That's the reasons why I asked these questions. Ms. Mahindaratne, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, can I have document number P577, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in fact, you referred to the fact that all -- that what occurred in the operations, with regard to fire contact and taking of prisoner of war being reported -- what you would see on your screen right now, Mr. Cvrk, is an overview of the reports submitted by the special police units, all the units, during the series of mop-up operations Oluja-Obruc. Now, what we have here is for date 21st August. You see that none of the units have met with fire contact with any enemy groups. There aren't any prisoners taken on 21st.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, if you could move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The 22nd. It was noted that none of the units had met with fire contact and there aren't any prisoners taken. And when I used the term "prisoners," I'm referring to members of the Serb military.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if you could go to page 3. And I believe the third block is darkened out. I think it's more clear on the English -- at least we would know what exactly it says. If could you get -- bring up the English document also at the same time. That -- that slot is redacted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What you would see from what is -- what we can read, there are no fire contact and no prisoners captured.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if you could go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: This is the 24th. It's the same: no fire contact; no prisoners captured.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: 25th; next page, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There is no fire contact. And there is one prisoner taken by your unit, which is the reference you just made.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if could you go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: 26th: there is only fire contact recorded against the Lucko Unit, and no fire contact with regard to any other units. No one captured.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There is just one fire contact recorded against the Primorje Gorski Unit. None of the other units have any contact. And, again, one person captured by your unit, as well as the other unit that had had fire contact.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if you could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, could we go back for one second to the previous page. At the bottom of this page, Mr. Cvrk, we find recorded that one person was captured. It's also recorded that there was one civilian. Does that mean that one person was captured and that one civilian person was found; or would it mean that one person was captured and that he was the civilian that was found there? Could you explain to us the structure of this report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As did I not draft this report, I can just assume that the person who was taken prisoner is not the same person who is registered as the civilian here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, if you didn't draft it, you could also assume the other way around, or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose that it is not one and the same person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And on what grounds do you suppose that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in the same table further down, in "prisoners," I see that there's just a dash. And then, on the right-hand side, there are seven civilians entered. So I suppose that the data was entered independently into each column.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But if none of the civilians were arrested, this is what you would expect, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But, likewise, under "prisoners," it says that there was one former JNA sergeant, and it says "several civilians." So I believe that the column "civilians" was registered independently of the column that includes those captured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation. Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, if you could go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: This is the 28th, and you will see there is no fire contact by any unit or -- and one person has been -- I'm sorry, no one captured.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if you could go to the next page, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Again, no one -- no fire contact. And Zadar-Knin Special Police Unit has captured one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And to the next page, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No fire contact by any units. Again, the Split Special Police Unit has captured one person.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No fire contact by any units. It's the same. No one captured.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Next page, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No fire contact. No one captured.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It's the same: No fire contact. No one captured.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Next page, please. This is the last -- last day of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No fire contact, and no one captured. So, Mr. Cvrk, in your statement you said that there were several fire contacts during the mop-ups. And today, a little while ago, you said that -- this is what you said: "I know that such contacts did occur and that there was a number of units who reported that kind of contacts to the special police sector." Now, we saw from the special police report itself, that only the Lucko Unit had reported fire contact on 26th. And there was, on the 27th, one other unit that had reported fire contact. So in your -- your -- in your testimony, you have exaggerated - haven't you? - by saying there were several contacts which several units had reported. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I can agree with you, because my recollection included the death of a member of special police which happened between the Operation Storm and the Operation Oluja-Obruc, which is not included in this report. I have no reason to doubt that the reports which you showed here are correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, we saw -- in fact, we just discussed that, on the 25th, your unit arrested a person, captured a person, and in fact the Chamber questioned you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could have P608, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, this is a report. This is your report, in fact, for that day, which you have submitted to the operation commander. In the second paragraph, you record that -- the capture of that prisoner. You said: "During the search of terrain, which was done in 13 groups of men and two official dogs ... the following civilian was found, and is suspected to have participated in the armed rebellion against the RH ..." There's the details of the civilian Luka Pasic, born 4th October, 1934, in Otok - and then the next word is illegible - resident in Pasic hamlet. "He was handed over for further processing to the Knin Police Station. All other persons found by the unit during the search had duly registered places of residence and passes issued by the military police." Now, my question is first: Was this place called Otok-Bender? Do you recall? If you don't remember, it's all right.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you with any precision. It's been a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That's okay. Now, can you please explain this "duly registered places of residence and passes" that you refer to in paragraph 4? What were those? In fact, one of the basis, as I understand from this document, for taking that person into custody is because he did not have these passes. What were those passes that you were looking for?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: What I wrote in this report was that the individuals found in the area searched by the unit had their place of residence registered, whereas, other individuals, who entered the area, were in possession of passes allowing them freedom of movement. Passes given to them by the military police. And this meant that all the individuals found in the area were legitimately there. To the best of my recollection, in order to enter, gain access to the area, and the date is the 26th August, one had to have an express authorisation to enter the area, especially in order to prevent unauthorised entry into the area. And that was one of the measures in force at the time, in order to prevent theft, looting, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now -- so, there -- as I understand you, there were two types of documentation: One was where the civilians had some documentation to show that they were -- they had a registered place of residence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were citizens, civilians, individuals who resided there. For the most part, they had proper documentation or were in the process of obtaining them. The other category of persons who were able to gain access to the area --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I will get to that other category. The first category: What were the documents in the course of the mop-ups? What were those documents that you would ask for which would establish a person's residence, which would establish that he was, in fact, legally a resident in the area? So what were you looking for, in terms of documentation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I do believe that, by that time, the 26th of August, the better part of the civilians found in the liberated area had already applied for Croatian documents or had certificates given to them by the UNHCR, certifying that they had been in the area before.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So they would have a certificate or some documentation received which would indicate that they had applied for documentation. That was the first category of people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, those passes, those -- -- those who did not have this documentation to show their residence, they had to have a pass to enter the area, is it -- is that what you -- that's what you just said?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, from this document -- your report indicates that those passes were issued by the military police.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what the report says, I do believe that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Are you able to tell the Trial Chamber what type of passes these were? Did it say that the person had been -- who had signed it, issued by what authority?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been an agency of the Croatian authorities that issued it. And I believe that the individuals who had passes were individuals who had lived in the area previously and were in possession of Croatian documents, as such. And the purpose of their travel there was to see their relatives or property.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So anyone who didn't have these type of -- two types of documents would be arrested for further verification; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I think that the check-points which were jointly manned by the Croatian police and the army prevented such individuals from entering the area. However, if they did manage to enter the area in one way or the other, it was up to us to report them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now what from the instructions? Who gave you the instructions about these passes, and what were those instructions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was discussed at the general briefing which we had prior to any sort of search operation. That was the only time we could have been told that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you -- could I please have document number 1393, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question for purposes of clarification. Mr. Cvrk, you were talking about passes issued by the military police. Would this be passes just valid for the duration of the search of the terrain; or would they have -- would they be issued especially for that day or that occasion; or would the passes be of a more general character? If you know. If you don't know, tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not 100 per cent sure, but I believe that these you were one-day passes, allowing an individual to enter the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that's -- my question was whether they were specific for that day of the search, or whether they would be -- one day could be during that search or could be at another day, validity only for one day. Could you tell us whether they were specifically for the search occasion or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the passes were issued regardless of the searches of the terrain. We happened to be there searching the area when these individuals were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which means that those persons who were not registered were not free to move without such a pass; is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. They were directed to obtain such passes as soon as possible. And I'm referring to the population found in the area at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, if I could have 65 ter 1393, please. For the record, Your Honours, this is an extract of the Exhibit P1240, which is already in evidence, which is the war record of the Zagreb Special Police Unit. 65 ter 1393.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvrk, you might recognise this document. This is a part of your war record, which is already in evidence, for the Zagreb Unit. Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did you write it yourself?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: A group of policemen wrote it. I didn't personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in -- if you see in the second paragraph you record as follows: "Since all Croatian villages and areas were burnt and destroyed, the action was carried out in the area mostly occupied by Serbs." Now, this is a record of your mop-up operations. And a little while ago I asked you if you had any information before your operations as to whether -- as to what -- what villages were Croatian and what villages were Serb villages, and you said that was not important, that that information was not provided, and you didn't even consider that aspect. So how is it that when you're writing this report you have reported that those burnt villages were Croatian villages? That's an inaccurate report, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a mis -- total mischaracterisation. The question Mr. Cvrk was asked was: Before the operation, were briefed on areas relating to Serb and Croat populations? And he said, No --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Mr. President, I don't think that that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... can I finish, please. MS. MAHINDARATNE -- should take place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... not two at a time. Do you speak any English, Mr. Cvrk? Do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that doesn't help us out. One second.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I could, Mr. President, proceed with the other questions and get to this just at the point of the break to save time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you move on and certainly from the first line expressed by Mr. Kuzmanovic, you know already what his concern is. Perhaps you could consider and perhaps -- when summarizing what the witness said a couple of minutes ago, to literally quote him on that matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I will do that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that we have no problems in mischaracterisation of the earlier testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That is satisfactory, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I will get to this in a moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, as you deem fit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvrk, were you -- or did you receive orders from General Markac regarding operations, mop-up operations, or the -- Storm, the initial attack itself. Did you receive, directly, orders from General Markac?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I received my orders from General Markac.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, were those orders given to you in writing or verbally?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: We all received elements of orders which had to do with our axis of attack. And I'm now referring to Operation Storm, because there was a generic order, and we received the elements that were relevant to our axes. As for Oluja-Obruc, we would be receiving orders for the following day. And they came from the special police sector.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter isn't sure about the last part.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you repeat your last few words, Mr. Cvrk. The interpreter didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: For Operation Oluja-Obruc, we received daily orders for the following day. And they were, for the most part, written by the special police sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in your testimony in your statement at paragraph 21 and 22 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, you're in -- you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just one word is missing in line 2 of page 30th. So maybe we could ask witness -- well, now it's in. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you see, miracles still happen. Yes. Assisted by our transcriber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 21 and 22 of your statement you say that, on every occasion and at every meeting you attended, General Mladen Markac emphasised the obligation to adhere to RH regulations and those of the international law of war. Now, did he reiterate those instructions regarding the international law of war at -- before he issued every order for every operation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you this with 100 per cent certainty, because there were such situations and attacks where we suffered casualties. What I can tell you with full certainty is that the units I commanded, as well as other units, before being introduced into Operation Storm, had to have gone through training on the international law of war and had to go through the textbooks, and I think this is something that the Trial Chamber is aware of.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Cvrk, you've already mentioned about your training. I'm not asking about your training. I'm asking about what General Markac told you. And this is what you have said: You said that on every occasion and at every meeting you attended, General Markac reminder you of these international law of war. And presumably what you are referring there is to -- how to treat civilians and prisoners of war. Now, my question to you is: Before he issued an order for an operation, a mop-up operation, did the reiterate these orders, these instructions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: We were specifically cautioned, before engaging in Operation Oluja-Obruc, about the civilians that we might come across. So this was the subject of every single briefing we had and every order we received.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So in every order you received, that reminder would be included. That's what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't claim that daily orders were written for Operation Oluja-Obruc, but we were cautioned about the presence of civilians in the areas we were supposed to search, and about the treatment that we were supposed to accord them at the briefings that we had.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in your written orders, were these instructions included, -- the written orders that you received for a specific operation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that we had written orders for Oluja-Obruc, but I think it was included in the general order for Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If I could call document P556.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And I can tell you, Mr. Cvrk, we do have a number of orders issued during Oluja-Obruc in evidence at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could have P556.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And this is not issued to you. This is -- because you were not involved in this specific mop-up operation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for information, P556 is not included in the list of exhibits to be used by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It is, Mr. President. As I -- probably Mr. Kuzmanovic has --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it P or D, because there is no P55 --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: P556 and P557 are included.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: 554, 560, 577; that's the order on my list that I received from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you please verify.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, if I could have a moment. It is not, Mr. President, in fairness to the Defence. I will therefore not call this document. Unless the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: This is a document [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course if Ms. Mahindaratne didn't call the document, then there is no issue anymore. If she would like to proceed, would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have an objection to that. I just wanted to have notice of it. And now, obviously, we have it. It's a document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you are free either to use it or not use it under the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Thank you, Mr. President. I will use it. Thank you, Mr. Kuzmanovic. Mr. Registrar, can we go back to the document P556.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, this is not an order issued to you, Mr. Cvrk. This is it an order issued to a different special police unit, because you were not involved in this specific mop-up operation. And can you read this order, and can you see that there is no instructions reminding the units as to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry to rise, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One -- let's first allow Ms. Mahindaratne to finish the question, and then we'll hear your objection, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now my question -- you will see that there is no such instruction.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: My question to you is: Now, did you receive any written orders regarding mop-up operations where such an instruction was included?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document deals with Sector North PU Karlovac, which is not part of this area that we're dealing with in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a document which is in evidence, and this is -- it relates to this part of the case as, not territory-wise, but to General Markac's command and control. And my question is very fair. I'm just reminding this witness, since he said he cannot recollect as to how the orders looked or whether he received, whether he received such an order, or -- as to whether he had received such instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would say it's, rather, background than directly applicable for the territory covered by the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvrk, can you tell the Trial Chamber if, in fact, you had received any written orders from Mr. Markac for mop-up operations, where you were reminded about your obligation to comply with international law.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sense of it being in an order, written order, for Oluja-Obruc, I cannot be sure. I cannot claim either way. I know that we were, though, cautioned about our duty to behave in a certain way, where clear procedure was defined. Now, whether this was in verbal or a written order, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. Going back to the issue -- the previous issue that I said I would get back to --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if could I have 65 ter 1393.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And while the document is coming up, Mr. Cvrk, let me remind you what you said this morning. I asked if you had been briefed, either prior to the commencement of Operation Storm itself or the mop-up operations, were you given any information as to which of the villages through which your unit moved advanced as to which of those villages were Croat villages or which was Serb villages. Were you given that information? And your response was: "Similarly to an attitude of the members of my unit which came from several ethnicities in terms of their origin, my attitude to them was like to any citizens of the Republic of Croatia, my attitude" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, you're reading.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. I think I will -- that was a long answer, which was not on point. My next question to you was: "Mr. Cvrk, you didn't quite answer my question. My question was not about your attitude. Whether any information was given to you as to what villages on the route through your axis were Croat villages or what were Serbs, whether that information was provided to you either by the special police sector command or the inner control branch, any intelligence information. That was my question. "Is that a yes or a no?" You say: "In that sense, no." That was your answer. Now, in this document, 65 ter 1393, you have reported that the villages that -- you say: "Since all Croatian villages and areas were burnt and destroyed, the action was carried out in the area mostly occupied by Serbs." So if you had not been given that information, Mr. Cvrk, how did you know that the villages and the area that were burnt were Croat villages, as opposed to Serb?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to say that the document you're referring to was, in fact, written as a narrative, almost a literary rendition of it. And I cannot, in any way, tie it with the actions that we talk in Operation Oluja-Obruc. There was a rendition of the events by one of the members of the special police. The description of the state of affairs and -- and the war path of my unit cannot be really tied in with this. And I'm sure that you will find nothing in the war record that contradicts what I said, and I said that the actions in Operation Oluja-Obruc were not related to an area that had suffered more or less damage but it, in fact, referred to an area where I was instructed to go and search.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So as I understand your testimony to be, what you're saying in that specific sentence is not correct. That was just written as a narrative, but there is no truth to that. That's what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Mahindaratne, let's try to -- I can understand that you are a bit confused by the answer of the witness because he used many words but didn't really answer your question. Earlier you said prior to the -- your operations, you were not informed about what were Serb villages, what were Croat villages. Now, in this report, a distinction is made between these two kind of villages. How did this information -- how was this information introduced, where you were not informed about it before the operation? Where does it come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For each and every operation in Oluja-Obruc, we received maps and indications as to where we were supposed to go. To me, as a commander, the fact that the area had suffered more or less damage did not matter as much. I had to go through an area as per the order. What the war record says is written more of a -- more as a narrative. And it reflects the personal view of the author of the war record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Personal view, I mean, it's an observation, whether a village is a Croat village or mainly Serbian-populated village. Do you know where the author of this document got this information from? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Believe me, I don't know. I think that this was his personal, general conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I accept that you say, I don't know where he got it from. That -- to characterise a village as of one or another ethnicity, to say that this is an overall conclusion, whereas, usually it is a fact which is based on other facts. But let's leave that apart. You do not know, and that's most important. Ms. Mahindaratne, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I tender this document. It's a part of Exhibit P1240, for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And it's not sufficient that we know what pages of -- do we need a duplicate here?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. It's just for the record I indicated that it is a part. It is not -- this document is not included in P1240, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is not included.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it needs an exhibit number. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document becomes Exhibit P2679. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? If not, P2679 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time. I have just one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Ms. Mahindaratne, forgive me for not immediately responding to numbers, but the author of this portion of the document is who exactly?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a part of the war record of the -- this witness's unit, Zagreb Special Police Unit. The exact author is not known.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a unit report.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It is an appropriate time for the break. You know that before breaks I'm usually interested in knowing how much time you would still need.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I believe less than a half-hour, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Less than half an hour. Mr. Mikulicic, could you give, already, an estimate, as matters stand now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: As matters stand now, I believe I will have one session, maybe less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider the times claimed and the times to be allowed. We'll have a break, and we'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvrk, now you testified yesterday that you were in Donji Lapac on 7th August, late evening, to report on your unit linking with the Gospic Military District units.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: This is, for the record, at transcript page 25378.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: To whom did you report to in Donji Lapac?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I found the chief of the special police sector in Donji Lapac, and that was Mr. Zeljko Sacic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And when you were asked about what you observed in Donji Lapac, this is what you say. You said: "There was quite obvious that a high degree of combat activity had taken place there. The command building and the police station had received several direct hits." What command building were you referring to in Donji Lapac?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was the police station building.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So there wasn't a separate command building. You were referring to the one police station; that's all?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was the police station, as it was the duty of other forces who were already there to deal with that, this is just my general recollection from the moments when I passed through the town, and this is what I confirmed here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, yesterday, you said, Mr. Cvrk, that you were in Donji Lapac until night-fall. And you say: "I spent some time this with the men from the battery that I referred to." And you also say that on the following morning at some 10.00 or 11.00 in the morning, you were invited to a coordination meeting of all special police unit commanders.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: This is at page 25379.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, where was that coordination meeting that you were supposed to report to on the following morning?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was held in Boricevac. There was a building next to the school, and there was a church very close by where we had the meeting. But whether this was -- this place where we had the meeting was a part of the school, I'm not sure. But the school and the church were certainly right next to that place.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And was Mr. Markac present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Markac was present at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And Mr. Sacic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: So was Mr. Sacic and most of us commanders of special police units.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So this was on the 8th August morning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I think that it was so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you also said that -- this is what you said. I'll read it to you. You said: "To my knowledge, most of the units of were disengaged, one by one, in succession; and, as far as I remember, until the end of the day, and I'm referring to the 9th of August, all of us had left the general area of Donji Lapac." So do I understand your testimony to be that to the end of 9th August, the units were in the area of Donji Lapac; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To the -- by the end of the 9th, according to my recollection, yes, that was so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recall where you spent the night of 7th August?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I spent the night between the 7th and the 8th in a place called Bruvno where I arrived very late in the even.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And your unit? Where was your unit stationed on the evening of 9th -- 7th August?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Between the 7th and the 8th, a part of the unit which was part of the rocket and artillery support for the special police were in the general area of Boricevci. And most of the members of the unit were in Bruvno.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvrk, did you see houses burning in Donji Lapac in the evening of 7th August?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a part of them. But I don't have a major recollection of Donji Lapac itself, because my activity on the 7th was focused towards Udbina, so that I do not remember all the developments in Donji Lapac except reports on linking up with forces from the Gospic Military District.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: But can you be a bit more specific? You said you recall "part of them." So about how many houses did you see burning when you saw? I mean, approximately 10, 20, more than that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, maybe up to ten facilities, not just houses, but, as far as I remember, it was one motel, and there was a truck burning which was hit at the very entrance to the town. So maybe up to ten various facilities or so, but I couldn't say that with 100 per cent certainty, because I was not focused on that at all at the time, because this was the zone of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, was the burning discussed at the meeting had you with Mr. Sacic in Donji Lapac? You know, did you all, at this, discuss as to what was going on, why there were property burning?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not. My discussion with Mr. Sacic was focused on the execution of the tasks that I had to, together with my colleagues, to link up with the Military District Gospic and in the direction of Udbina. I came there to report to him that we managed to link up with them, that we linked up with the 9th Brigade before Udbina. And, thus, we accomplished our task. So the contents of my discussion with Mr. Sacic was mainly focused on the execution of this particular task.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know as to who burnt those houses, at least, Mr. -- at least today?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from general information, or from what I could glean here and there, it was a place where we linked up with parts of the Croatian Army, and it's possible that some problems resulted from that. And during the preparation for my testimony, I was informed about the reactions of the special police command to this. But as for my knowledge from that time, when these events were taking place, I do not have it. I know that this problem did occur. I even saw some of the documents discussing these problems during my preparation for my testimony. And I could see from what the command of special police did that this happened, but I didn't take any part in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So during your preparations, the Defence team showed you documentation and informed you about the evidence regarding what happened in Donji Lapac?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they informed me about the documents which are enclosed and which are connected with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And were you also informed as to, you know -- earlier on you said that you were shown photographs about special police members being -- special police members taken in Gracac. Were you also informed about the evidence relating to those photographs, what has transpired in the testimonies here?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I was shown these photographs, and as you asked me previously, I saw this on the Internet when I was in Zagreb. When I returned from here, I saw the statement of Mr. Pavlovic in connection with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So you were shown Mr. Pavlovic's statement in the preparation for this testimony today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not during the preparation. But I found it on the Internet. I saw his statement on the Internet. That was at the time when I was in Zagreb, and not here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I seek, on one point, clarification, Ms. Mahindaratne. These photographs, they were shown to you during your preparation for your testimony; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you briefly describe what you saw in these photographs? Not in detail but ... was it persons, was it houses, was it -- what did you see on the photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were photographs depicting special police members in vehicles and standing by some houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember the colour of those vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Because, as far as I can remember, the photographs were black and white.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then it's difficult to identify the colour. That's ... Were these trucks or vehicles for persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One truck and a number of passenger vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One of them showing someone to -- who is about to jump-start the passenger vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Just one other question about Donji Lapac. Now, you said you didn't pay attention to what happened in Donji Lapac but you were informed in your preparation about the documentation and the evidence. Were you informed that there has been some discussion as to who perpetrated the crimes in Donji Lapac? About -- you, in fact, referred to the linking up with the army. Were you specifically informed of that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Was I specifically informed about that at the time, during the Operation Storm, while it was in progress? Was that your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, no, during your preparations with the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: During the preparation, we discussed that, whether a unit of Croatian Army entered Donji Lapac and several problems arose, as a result of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, can I have P586, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, before we look at that, could you, please, further explore what the several problems were that arose. Could you give us further information? You said you discussed it and several problems arose as a result of that. What problems arose?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mostly, several facilities were torched when this unit entered Donji Lapac. This is what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And you were told that by -- during the preparation for testimony by the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in this way the Defence wanted to prepare me concerning absolutely all events connected with the military and police Operation Storm and the area through which the special police was moving. So I think it was their general intention and that they told me that in order to remind me of the events in Donji Lapac. So, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And were you -- I'm going show you two documents, Mr. Cvrk. If could you just quickly tell the Trial Chamber if you have seen these two documents during preparation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if could I have P586, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see this document during preparation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Not this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can I have D556, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Were you shown this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, no, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: When you say "generally speaking," is it that you can't remember or ...

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not 100 per cent sure, but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, until the Defence informed you of the -- of the situation in Donji Lapac, were you aware of any facts about what really happened in Donji Lapac, resulting from experience during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN CVRK[Resumed]
